newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria winds up violence-free vote on constitution.
newsitem.headline: Algeria winds up violence-free vote on constitution.

text.p: Algeria's polls closed on Thursday at 8 p.m. (1900) after a peaceful vote on a constitutional referendum that would ban Islamic political parties.

More than two hours before polls closed, official figures reported that nearly three-quarters of Algeria's 16.4 million eligible voters had cast ballots despite threats by Moslem militants to kill anyone who voted.

More than 735,000 expatriate voters voted between Saturday and Thursday. More than 500,000 members of armed and security forces voted on Monday so they would be free to guard voters during the official polls.
Official media said voting was taking place peacefully and there were no reports of violence.

The national turnout was 71.94 percent at about 6 p.m (1700 GMT), compared to 65.82 percent in last year's presidential election at the same time, according to interior ministry figures reported by state-run radio.
However, Algerian radio said turnout was lower at around 22 percent in two northeastern Berber provinces where a Berber-dominated party had called for a boycott, according to the same figures.
Moslem rebels, waging a five-year guerrilla war against the North African country's secular government, had vowed to disrupt the poll and warned Algerians not to vote.

Opposition parties either called for a boycott or urged a "no" vote on the changes, which would strengthen the position of President Liamine Zeroual and bar Islamic fundamentalists from seeking election.
